Post-investment EBIT is two hundred and fifty million dollars, existing shares total ninety million, and tax is forty percent. What is the EPS difference, debt minus equity, in dollars per share?

follow_up.question: Does higher EPS prove that the debt option creates more value?
follow_up.reference: EPS ignores important differences in financial risk and the required return on equity. Evaluate investment value and financing costs separately.

instances.text: Consider a manufacturer. Raise 800 million dollars with 6 percent debt or new shares at 40 dollars. Post-investment EBIT is 258 million dollars, existing shares total 100 million, and tax is 25 percent. What is the EPS difference, debt minus equity, in dollars per share?
instances.spoken_text: Consider a manufacturer. Raise eight hundred million dollars with six percent debt or new shares at forty dollars. Post-investment EBIT is two hundred and fifty-eight million dollars, existing shares total one hundred million, and tax is twenty-five percent. What is the EPS difference, debt minus equity, in dollars per share?

follow_up.question: What changes if the financing occurs halfway through the year?
follow_up.reference: Interest and new share count must reflect the relevant timing and weighted-average conventions. Using full-year interest with half-year shares would create an inconsistent comparison.

instances.text: Consider a distributor. Raise 450 million dollars with 10 percent debt or new shares at 45 dollars. Post-investment EBIT is 205 million dollars, existing shares total 50 million, and tax is 25 percent. What is the EPS difference, debt minus equity, in dollars per share?
instances.spoken_text: Consider a distributor. Raise four hundred and fifty million dollars with ten percent debt or new shares at forty-five dollars. Post-investment EBIT is two hundred and five million dollars, existing shares total fifty million, and tax is twenty-five percent. What is the EPS difference, debt minus equity, in dollars per share?

follow_up.question: Why does the interest tax shield matter to the EPS comparison?
follow_up.reference: Deductible interest reduces the after-tax cost of debt when the tax benefit can be used. Ignoring that benefit understates earnings under debt financing.

follow_up.question: What if equity were issued at a higher price for the same funding need?
follow_up.reference: Fewer new shares would be required. That would reduce dilution and improve the equity-funded EPS, holding operating profit fixed.
